parsed.explanation: Combined national and Oklahoma regime combines birth-sex facilities, binary documents and entry fraud exposure, adult and minor care bans in public facilities, sports exclusion, no state anti-discrimination or hate-crime cover, and birth-sex custody with conversion practices, plus documented immigration-custody abuse. Federal courts, injunctions, federal hate-crime law and private care/facilities limit severity; there is no credible execution and imprisonment is not automatic, but universal exposures compound below the 0.45-0.55 tiers.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex passport policy stopped new X markers from Feb 2025, Supreme Court allowed restrictions Nov 2025; entry cable directs refusal for document discrepancy casting doubt on sex and possible permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation. Oklahoma bars birth-certificate marker changes.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic, with limited waivers. Passport policy is in litigation.
entry_documents.interaction: A foreign passport discrepancy can trigger secondary inspection, refusal, or investigation, converting a document issue into detention or lifetime ineligibility risk at the border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Oklahoma executive order applies birth-sex definitions to incarceration; national corrections bureau from 2026 adopted conversion practices including hair cutting and hormone removal. Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of transgender men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Federal courts have blocked or enjoined several national orders; no documented visitor-specific custody case is in the dossier and Not documented. for Oklahoma detention conditions.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest or immigration detention exposes the traveller to birth-sex placement and care denial inside custody, where remedy is slow and reporting of transgender prisoners stopped in 2025.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars government-funded facilities inconsistent with birth sex. Oklahoma requires school facilities by original birth certificate and applies birth-sex definitions to state-owned bathrooms and changing rooms; four states make certain bathroom use criminal, illustrated by a 2025 capitol arrest and 24 hours in men's ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states, 4 other jurisdictions and capital district have no mapped ban, but Oklahoma is in the restrictive group. Private facilities are not covered by the cited bans.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Universal, unavoidable exposure in schools, government buildings and, if detained, custody; trespass requires willful entry and refusal to depart in the cited state statute, not automatic arrest on entry.

care_services.exposure: Oklahoma SB904, effective 14 May 2026, bars public funds, Medicaid and state-owned facilities from gender-affirming surgeries, blockers and hormones for minors and adults, with employee misdemeanour liability. Earlier law bans minor care and government funding for transition services.
care_services.protection: Private facilities with private insurance or out-of-pocket payment remain available; exemptions cover counselling, some medications, intersex care, complications and emergency treatment to prevent death or major impairment.
care_services.interaction: A traveller needing routine hormone continuity may be denied at public or state facilities and must use private care; staff criminal liability can chill even exempt care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders frame gender identity as ideology, direct law-enforcement investigation of schools, and a May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises radically pro-transgender groups. Oklahoma has no state gender-identity discrimination protection and sports bans exclude transgender women and girls.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity in federal court; a 2020 Supreme Court ruling prohibits workplace gender-identity discrimination nationally; several orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Efficient enforcement of hostile facility, document and care rules is itself exposure; federal protection does not cancel state facility bans, custody placement or entry screening.

minors_guardians.exposure: Oklahoma SB615 requires school bathrooms and changing rooms by birth certificate; sports bans exclude transgender students; minor gender-affirming care is banned; national order directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition including pronouns. A travelling minor faces facility, school and care denial.
minors_guardians.protection: SB904 imposes no penalties on patients; counselling and emergency care are exempt. No documented guardian investigation of a travelling family is provided.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parents may face loss of public care, school placement by birth sex, and provider or school liability, forcing private payment, missed schooling or separation of care from the child.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Oklahoma has no state hate-crime cover for gender identity. Resident incidents include 2018 death threats against a 12-year-old and the 2024 Nex Benedict death after a school-bathroom beating; no visitor-specific violence is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime prosecution remains available. One city bans gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations; three others only in city employment.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Resident violence is a weak, dated signal for visitor risk, but absence of state recourse and at-will employment limit practical remedy if a traveller is harassed or denied service.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Multiple national orders and passport restrictions remain in litigation; Oklahoma HB1225 was pending signature on 6 May 2026, driver's licence current status is not documented, and the July 2026 travel-risk grade for Oklahoma is not stated.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, injunctions and federal courts provide real but unresolved recourse; legal-aid FAQ guidance exists for passport and document rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies may work over months or years, after a short-stay traveller has been refused entry, denied facilities or care, or detained, so they do not neutralise immediate exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar or slightly lower: both impose birth-sex prison housing and criminal facility exposure with slow remedies and short sentences. Oklahoma is comparable because custody conversion practices and immigration-custody abuse are documented, though organised raids and frequent prison assaults are not documented for visitors.

Materially lower: the 0.55 anchor has discretionary secondary screening and administrative refusal with appeal and consular access. Here document discrepancy can lead to refusal plus fraud ineligibility, and compounding facility, care, sports, custody and no-state-protection rules exceed a single screening exposure.

Far lower: the 0.85 anchor recognises trans and nonbinary passports, trains officers, provides legal aid and compensation. This regime stops X passports, mandates birth-sex facilities and custody, bans public care for adults and minors, and lacks state-level protection, the opposite operative features.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one interacting system: binary national documents and entry screening can out and refuse the visitor; inside Oklahoma, birth-sex rules govern schools, state facilities, sports, public care and any custody; staff liability and absent state protections make private alternatives the only documented route. Minors face the same facility and care bars plus school enforcement. Federal litigation and hate-crime law are real mitigations but operate after immediate loss of entry, facilities, medication or liberty, and do not pre-empt state enforcement. That combination of universal exposures with severe custody consequences, short of routine imprisonment or execution, supports a low-0.30s rating.
